Language and the mind are intertwined. The mind creates the symbols (objects - nouns, actions - verbs, states - adjectives, etc.) first, and then attaches words to them later. If the first part of that process is weak, the second part will appear to be broken.

I think this first part is very weak in the African mind because they never developed written language. Without a writing system, the vocabulary of a language stays rather small since the words must be retained in the minds of the speakers and passed from generation to generation orally. An exceptionally bright stone-age African whose mind produced twice as many symbols as his culture had words for would not make much use of this extra mental capacity. If he couldn't get the rest of his tribe to start using the new concepts that he was creating, those concepts would be lost. With a written language, the number of words expands dramatically, as concepts can be spread over a much greater distance both spatially and temporally. A bright man reading a book written by another bright man 200 years in the past and 1000 miles away, can make use of the concepts of a person he never could have possibly spoken to orally. Written language is essentially an intelligence bootstrapping method, which actively promotes intelligence. I propose that hundreds of generations of human evolution with written language is one of if not the largest factor that explains the intelligence gap between Africans and non-Africans.
